division_name: The Adventure Of The Engineer’S Thumb

characters.name: Victor Hatherley
characters.note: Young hydraulic engineer, narrator of his own ordeal; the morning patient who brings the case to Watson and Holmes. Only one Hatherley in the division; he is the Hatherley of the title.

characters.name: Dr. Watson
characters.note: Narrator of the story, a doctor with a civil practice near Paddington Station who brings Hatherley to Holmes; appears throughout as the first-person observer.

characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.note: Consulting detective in his Baker Street rooms, lounging in a dressing-gown; Watson's friend who solves the case by reasoning.

characters.name: Colonel Lysander Stark
characters.note: Thin, emaciated man of about forty with a German accent, who hires Hatherley under false pretences and tries to kill him in the press; the chief criminal, a coiner.

characters.name: Elise
characters.note: Pretty young woman in a rich dark dress, apparently Stark's wife or companion, who warns Hatherley and saves him from the press; speaks broken English.

characters.name: Mr. Ferguson
characters.note: Short, thick-set man with a chinchilla beard, Stark's secretary and manager; a fellow-countryman who helps carry the unconscious Hatherley away.

characters.name: Inspector Bradstreet
characters.note: Inspector of Scotland Yard who accompanies Holmes and Hatherley to Eyford to pursue the gang.

characters.name: Jeremiah Hayling
aliases: the missing engineer named in the advertisement
characters.note: Hydraulic engineer aged twenty-six, reported missing a year earlier after leaving his lodgings; a earlier victim of Stark's press, not present on stage.

characters.name: The guard
characters.note: Railway guard from Paddington who brings Hatherley to Watson's consulting-room at dawn.

characters.name: The maid
characters.note: Watson's maid who wakes him to announce the visitors.

characters.name: The station-master
characters.note: Station-master at Eyford who reports the fire at Dr. Becher's house.

characters.name: The porter
characters.note: Single night porter at Eyford Station who sees Hatherley arrive and later answers his questions.

characters.name: The driver
characters.note: Unnamed driver of the chestnut horse and closed carriage that takes Hatherley from Eyford to the house; never seen.

locations.name: Watson's consulting-room
locations.note: Watson's consulting-room near Paddington where Hatherley first appears at dawn with his bandaged hand.</note>

locations.name: Baker Street rooms
locations.note: Holmes's sitting-room in Baker Street where he eats breakfast and hears Hatherley's story.

locations.name: Hatherley's chambers, Victoria Street
locations.note: Hatherley's professional chambers, third floor, 16A Victoria Street, where Stark calls on him.

locations.name: Eyford house (Dr. Becher's)
locations.note: Isolated, whitewashed old house seven or more miles from Eyford in Berkshire, containing the hydraulic press; later burned down. Known later as Dr. Becher's house.

locations.name: Eyford Station
locations.note: Small station in Berkshire where Hatherley arrives at night and later returns at dawn.

locations.name: The garden and rose-bushes
locations.note: Garden of the house beneath the bedroom window, where Hatherley falls and faints among the rose-bushes.

locations.name: Reading
locations.note: Town where Hatherley changes trains and where the gang's carts were seen heading.

locations.name: Scotland Yard
locations.note: Police headquarters where Holmes and Hatherley go before travelling to Eyford.

brief.tone: Tense, claustrophobic Victorian mystery: a clammy, secretive country house, rising dread in the press scene, and dry, wry detection in London.
depiction_rules: Show the hydraulic press's descending ceiling as a threat but do not depict the mutilation graphically; the bandaged bloodied hand may be shown restrained.
Holmes is shown in his dressing-gown and armchair, smoking, with heavy-lidded composure.
Stark should be drawn gaunt and sharp-faced, with a bright, suspicious gaze.
Elise appears only at the doorway and window, beautiful and frightened, never fully revealed as a villain.
No modern machinery; the press is wooden-walled with an iron floor and water cylinders.

era.name: Late Victorian England, summer 1889
era.people: English professionals and tradesmen; a German-speaking foreign couple and an Englishman in Berkshire country houses; railway officials and Scotland Yard inspectors.
era.dress: Frock coats, waistcoats, tweed suits and caps for men; dark rich gowns for women; Holmes in a dressing-gown at home.
era.buildings_and_objects: Terraced London townhouses with consulting-rooms, Baker Street lodgings, gas-lit and oil-lamp-lit rooms, a dilapidated country house with bare upper floors, whitewashed walls, and a small rural station.
era.technology: Steam railways and hansom cabs, hydraulic presses, oil lamps and candles, ordnance maps and compasses; no telephone in the story, no electric light, no motor car.
